subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Pompeii's Forgotten Neighbor: Herculaneum
description: A 60-second lesson on Pompeii's Forgotten Neighbor: Herculaneum.

hook.text: Everyone knows Pompeii. Fewer know its neighbor Herculaneum, which was even better preserved — under 60 feet of rock.

buildup.text: While Pompeii was buried in ash, Herculaneum was entombed by a pyroclastic surge that carbonized everything instantly.

discovery.text: The extreme heat preserved wood, food, fabric, and even a library of carbonized scrolls still being read today.

twist.text: 300 skeletons were found on the beach — people waiting for boats that never came as the eruption overtook them.

climax.text: AI is now reading the burnt scrolls using X-ray scanning. Lost works of ancient philosophy are being recovered.

punchline.text: A volcano burned a library. Two thousand years later, AI is reading the ashes.

quiz.question: How is modern technology recovering Herculaneum's burnt scrolls?
options: Chemical treatments are unrolling and bleaching the scrolls
AI reads the carbonized text using X-ray scanning
3D printing recreates the scrolls from fragment photographs

details.summary: Herculaneum, buried deeper than Pompeii by volcanic mudflows from Vesuvius in 79 CE, preserves organic materials — wood, food, textiles, scrolls — that ash alone could not save.
details.whyItMatters: Herculaneum is in many ways better preserved than Pompeii — upper stories, wooden furniture, and organic materials survive. Its buried library, now being read by AI, could contain lost works of Greek philosophy.
takeaways: Buried deeper than Pompeii by volcanic mudflows preserving organic materials
Carbonized papyrus scrolls may contain lost ancient literature
Multi-story buildings and wooden furniture survive intact

faq.question: Why is Herculaneum less famous than Pompeii?
faq.answer: Herculaneum was buried under 20 meters of hardened volcanic rock, making excavation extremely difficult and expensive. Only about a quarter has been uncovered. Most of the ancient city lies beneath modern Ercolano, preventing further excavation. Pompeii's easier access made it more famous.

faq.question: What is the Villa of the Papyri and its library?
faq.answer: A luxurious seaside villa contained a library of about 1,800 carbonized papyrus scrolls — the only intact library surviving from antiquity. Most contain Epicurean philosophy. AI-assisted X-ray imaging is now reading scrolls that cannot be physically unrolled, potentially revealing lost Greek texts.
